stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Universal Music is launching an AI music platform with ElevenLabs
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Universal Music Group is launching a new AI music platform.
The platform will enable users to create remixes and mashups using licensed music from the UMG catalog.
The development is a multiyear licensing partnership with ElevenLabs, an AI voice synthesis specialist.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'llama'.
The primary use case demonstrated is 'text-generation' within the NLP pipeline.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks requiring context gathering and tool use on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
The updated engine also contributes to higher quality output from the language models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with popular local LLM runners.

stories.title: Slack can now vibe-code interactive charts and reports inside chats
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Slack is integrating 'Slackforce Surfaces' to allow users to build complex tools directly within chat.
The new AI feature enables users to describe desired outputs (charts, reports, dashboards) to a Slackbot.
The AI gathers necessary data from connected apps like Google Drive and Salesforce to generate the content.

stories.title: Schools are catching on to Big Tech’s playbook
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Big Tech companies are actively influencing K-12 education by providing AI-related curriculum and resources to schools.
The narrative being pushed is that proficiency in these new technologies is essential for students' future career success.
This trend represents a significant industry shift where tech giants are partnering with educational institutions to drive adoption.

stories.title: Electric air taxis get the green light for test flights in Texas
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: A new federal program is launching in Texas to test electric, hybrid-electric, and autonomous aircraft.
The testing is commencing before the final regulatory rules for this Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) technology are established.
The FAA's eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) has selected eight state-led initiatives for this testing.

stories.title: Panic builds over bankrupt Spirit’s looming data sale to Google
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy proceedings are linked to a potential data sale to Google.
The news raises concerns about the commodification of personal data during corporate distress.
The article frames the situation as a potential 'land grab' in the AI era, questioning data acquisition ethics.

stories.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
stories.author: Mike Zheng Shou
bullet_points: Introduces Show-Harness, an Embodied Harness designed to bridge the gap between high-level VLM intelligence and low-level robot control.
The system allows Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to 'play' robots by reasoning over discrete, semantic action units.
It uses embodiment-specific interpreters to deterministically translate abstract semantic intents into concrete, local robot actions.

stories.title: Semigroup-JEPA: Latent Dynamics Consistency for Zero-Shot Physics Generalization
stories.author: John Sous
bullet_points: Introduces SemiGroup-JEPA (SG-JEPA) to enhance Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models.
Addresses a key limitation of JEPA by integrating physics parameters into the temporal model via action-conditioning.
Aims to improve the models' ability to learn physics and generate physically realistic dynamics for zero-shot generalization.

stories.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Bo Xu
bullet_points: ConvMem proposes a new approach, Convolutional Memory, to overcome the fixed context limitations of Large Language Models (LLMs).
It aims to address the latency and high training costs associated with existing sequential context extension methods (like MemAgent).
The research focuses on enabling LLMs to handle extremely long contexts more efficiently than current state-of-the-art techniques.

stories.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
stories.author: Agoritsa Polyzou
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing and reproducing sensitive or undesirable training data.
Proposes 'Layer-Selective Unlearning' as a method to selectively forget specific knowledge without full model retraining.
Aims to improve the robustness of unlearning techniques against deployment changes like quantization, which often cause knowledge leakage.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to accurately measure enterprise AI systems based on their serving route, rather than just model identifiers.
Addresses the industry problem where current benchmarks only score advertised model identifiers, ignoring crucial deployment factors like serving route and precision.
The protocol includes a preflight check to verify execution contracts and a scoring rule that accounts for reliability.

stories.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning
stories.author: Yi Zhou
bullet_points: Proposes a novel framework to enhance LLMs for geometric reasoning, addressing a key weakness in current AI.
The framework integrates a 'Geometric Vision Parser' to translate visual diagrams into a format usable by LLMs.
Claims the pure LLM approach, when augmented, can achieve performance comparable to complex, computationally intensive LMMs on geometry tasks.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Meta’s Muse AI works and creeps me out
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta has released its new AI assistant, Muse, signaling a deeper push into AI-powered productivity tools.
Muse is designed to automate routine tasks such as online shopping, email management, and trip planning.
The article includes a hands-on review, offering a user perspective on the tool's performance and implications.

stories.title: LinkedIn beats "BrowserGate" lawsuits over scanning users' Chrome extensions
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: LinkedIn successfully defended against lawsuits concerning its scanning of users' Chrome extensions.
The judge dismissed the lawsuits, ruling that the plaintiffs failed to demonstrate a genuine privacy violation.
The case highlights ongoing legal scrutiny regarding how major platforms monitor user activity within browser extensions.

stories.title: Europe will go it alone on Venus mission after NASA yanks radar instrument
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: Europe is pursuing an independent Venus mission following NASA's decision to withdraw a radar instrument.
The shift suggests potential realignment of international space collaborations, possibly involving China.
The news reflects broader trends of potential changes or cancellations within NASA's partnership structure.

stories.title: Android can now securely migrate your logins between password managers
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Android now supports secure migration of login credentials between password managers.
The feature is currently limited in terms of application support.
Google has indicated that broader app support is planned for future updates.

stories.title: China’s drone supremacy shows in airlifting bodies and food after Nepal flood disaster
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: DJI drones are being utilized in Nepal for disaster relief efforts following severe flooding.
The drones, already used in high-altitude operations like Mount Everest camps, are performing critical tasks like airlifting supplies and bodies.
The incident highlights the practical application and growing role of drone technology in humanitarian aid and emergency response.

stories.title: Four groups caught using the same Chrome and Windows exploit kit
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Multiple threat groups were found utilizing an identical exploit kit targeting Chrome and Windows.
The vulnerability exploitation is linked to a 'patch gap' in system updates.
The rapid advancement of AI in discovering vulnerabilities is cited as a contributing factor to the threat landscape.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to measure enterprise AI systems based on their serving route rather than just model identifiers.
Addresses the industry problem where benchmarks only score advertised model identifiers, ignoring crucial deployment factors like serving route and precision.
The protocol includes a preflight check to verify execution contracts and a scoring rule that accounts for reliability.

stories.title: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
stories.author: Haifeng Wang
bullet_points: JarvisGUI addresses a gap in current AI agent evaluation by focusing on cross-device GUI interactions.
It tackles complex real-world workflows requiring state maintenance and coordination across heterogeneous platforms.
The research highlights that existing benchmarks are too limited by focusing only on single-device, static tasks.

stories.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs
stories.author: Eray Tüzün
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of unbounded memory growth and retrieval degradation in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Introduces 'Fortunate Recall' (FR), an ontology-driven policy layer for managing memory lifecycles.
Classifies personal facts into a behavioral ontology (10+1 categories) to apply tailored retention policies like differential temporal decay.

stories.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization
stories.author: Abhisek Dash
bullet_points: The paper investigates the viability of using Foundation Models (specifically VLMs) for consistent online content moderation.
It compares two methods for guiding these models: instruction-driven (reasoning from policy rules) versus example-driven (learning from examples).
The research addresses the critical challenge of operationalizing increasingly complex content moderation policies.

stories.title: Cross-Model Agreement as a Deployment-Time Reliability Signal for Automatic Polyp Segmentation
stories.author: Jitin Singla
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world problem in medical AI: silent failures of segmentation models during inference where ground truth is unavailable.
Introduces Referee-Based Quality Estimation (RBQE), a novel, reference-free framework to measure model reliability by comparing a primary model against an independent 'referee' model.
Validated on a standardized external benchmark (1,223 images) derived from multiple public datasets, indicating practical relevance in colonoscopy applications.

stories.title: Learning with Covariance Matrices: Principal Component Analysis Meets Learning with Graphs
stories.author: Alejandro Ribeiro
bullet_points: Introduces Covariance Neural Networks (VNNs), a novel approach combining GNNs with covariance matrices.
Addresses a gap in existing GNN theory by incorporating data-driven nuances inherent in covariance matrices.
Highlights the broad applicability of covariance matrices across various scientific and data domains.

stories.title: Deep Learning-Based Detection of Electrical Faults and Power Quality Disturbances in Aerospace Power Systems
stories.author: Berker Peköz
bullet_points: Addresses the need for fault detection in high-frequency (400 Hz) aerospace power systems, moving beyond traditional 50/60 Hz grid models.
Introduces a hardware-aware deep learning framework specifically designed for multiclass detection of electrical faults and power quality disturbances.
Utilizes a high-fidelity simulation model inspired by real-world aerospace architectures, such as the Boeing 787.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to accurately measure enterprise AI systems.
Argues that current evaluations incorrectly focus on model identifiers rather than the full serving route and system capabilities.
The protocol includes a preflight check and a reliability-inclusive scoring rule to address measurement errors.

stories.title: Building Multilingual Bridges: Data Mixing as the Pillar of Generalization for In-Language Reasoning
stories.author: Julia Kreutzer
bullet_points: Current reasoning language models exhibit strong English-centric bias, limiting accessibility for non-English speakers.
The research proposes 'Data Mixing' as a core technique to improve multilingual generalization in reasoning models.
The goal is to advance 'L2 reasoning,' enabling models to reason consistently in the language of the prompt.

stories.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Bo Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the context length limitations inherent in current Large Language Models (LLMs).
Proposes 'ConvMem,' a convolutional memory approach to handle long-context reasoning.
Aims to overcome the high latency and complex RL training requirements of existing sequential memory methods.

stories.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization
stories.author: Abhisek Dash
bullet_points: The paper investigates the reliability of Foundation Models (specifically VLMs) in moderating complex online content.
It compares two methods for guiding model behavior: instruction-driven (reasoning from policy) versus example-driven (learning from examples).
The research addresses the critical industry challenge of consistently operationalizing nuanced content moderation policies.

stories.title: Retrofitting Code Using LLMs to Support Exceptional Behavior
stories.author: Milos Gligoric
bullet_points: Proposes a novel task to automatically retrofit existing code with Exception Related Code (ERC).
ERC (try/catch, throw statements, etc.) is crucial for handling exceptional states in software but is tedious to write manually.
The method uses Large Language Models (LLMs) guided by Exceptional Behavior Tests (EBTs) to perform the retrofitting.

stories.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
stories.author: Mounîm A. El Yacoubi
bullet_points: Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) are advancing rapidly in video understanding tasks.
The high computational and memory cost of VideoLLMs, which scales with frame count, limits real-world deployment.
The paper surveys various inference-efficiency mechanisms designed to address these resource constraints.

stories.title: Shopify is moving from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin
stories.author: fnthawar2
bullet_points: Shopify is undergoing a significant technology shift in its mobile development strategy.
The company is migrating away from React Native.
The new native development stack will utilize Swift (for iOS) and Kotlin (for Android).

stories.title: The Deathray: A simple way for an untrusted site to freeze a Mac
stories.author: auberonedu
bullet_points: A vulnerability named 'Deathray' allows untrusted websites to potentially freeze macOS.
The exploit targets a specific mechanism within the operating system.
This represents a security risk related to web browsing on Apple devices.

stories.title: Technique for Manipulating Satellite Photos Now Reveals Ancient Images (2025)
stories.author: gumby
bullet_points: A technique originally developed for manipulating satellite photos is now capable of revealing ancient images.
The underlying technology appears to be a spinoff from NASA research.
The announcement links to both a technical paper (DecorrelationStretch.pdf) and a NASA technology transfer page.

stories.title: Rust Is Tier-1 Language at Microsoft
stories.author: rustfoundation.org via mmastrac
bullet_points: Microsoft has officially designated Rust as a Tier-1 language within its ecosystem.
This signifies a major commitment by a large tech player to adopting Rust for critical systems.
The move reflects the growing industry trend toward using memory-safe languages like Rust for performance-critical applications.

stories.title: Forgejo 16.0.4 has a critical security bug fix (RCE - Remote Code Execution)
stories.author: codeberg.org via brn
bullet_points: Forgejo, a self-hosted Git service, has released version 16.0.4.
This update addresses a critical security vulnerability.
The vulnerability is classified as Remote Code Execution (RCE), requiring immediate attention from users.

stories.title: AI Is Already Better at Coding Than Most Software Developers
stories.author: sylwia-lask
bullet_points: The article posits that AI is achieving coding proficiency surpassing many human developers.
It argues that coding itself is not the most critical skill in software development.
The piece suggests a shift in the value proposition of human developers away from pure coding.

stories.title: The Verification Bottleneck in AI-Generated Software
stories.author: kenwalger
bullet_points: AI code generation speed is accelerating rapidly.
The primary challenge is ensuring the correctness and reliability of AI-generated code.
The article addresses the 'verification bottleneck' in modern AI software development.

stories.title: Beyond LLMs: How World Models Are Changing Generative Media
stories.author: blackgirlbytes
bullet_points: The article discusses the shift in generative AI beyond Large Language Models (LLMs) to World Models.
World Models aim to provide a more comprehensive, predictive understanding of the world, similar to human cognition.
The introduction uses a relatable analogy (a toddler's reaction to milk/water) to illustrate predictive capability.
